A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIM-SDE, with matching authors, core architecture and canonical experiments. All pages, including appendices, are readable; the revised title, organization and experimental scope do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SDE estimation, simulated-path comparisons, real-world evaluations and motion forecasting results in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 reports original canonical, Lorenz and real-world experiments, together with finetuning results and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: v1 uses the pretrained model exclusively in zero-shot mode. v2 adds target-data finetuning through likelihood optimization for dense observations and simulation-based transition-error minimization for sparse observations (Appendix D.4, Equations 34–35). These substantially extend the procedure, while the core transformer architecture and weighted pretraining objective remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds Lorenz dynamics and Facebook/Tesla stock-price datasets, retains the seven original canonical systems and oil/wind datasets, and removes human-motion forecasting. Training coverage also changes: v1 includes random function compositions, whereas v2 uses polynomial SDEs and additionally tests degree-four polynomial training in an ablation.

E2.justification: LatentSDE becomes an evaluated comparator for Lorenz and all four real-world datasets, including the retained oil/wind comparisons previously involving only BISDE. Removing motion forecasting also removes v1 Table 4's literature-sourced comparisons with GPDM, VGPLVM, DTSBN-S, npODE, NeuralODE and ODE2VAE variants. SparseGP and BISDE remain in the canonical comparisons.

E3.justification: Pretraining changes from 700K SDEs with default observation spacing 0.08 to 600K with spacings 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 (v2 Table 4). Canonical evaluation removes spacing 0.01 and adds noise-corrupted settings. New experiments introduce finetuning budgets, Lorenz initial-condition tests and model/data/context-size controls. Finetuned FIM-SDE and LatentSDE are compared after 100 and 5000 iterations, respectively.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's observation-spacing comparisons, v2 adds controlled noise robustness tests and actual ablations of joint model/data scaling, polynomial degree and evaluation context size (Appendix H). Lorenz experiments test initial-distribution shifts and compare finetuning with training from scratch; Figure 3 and Table 9 add convergence analyses.

E5.justification: Canonical MMD reporting retains five independent datasets and mean/standard-deviation summaries. v2 adds standard deviations across five cross-validation folds for real-world results, replacing v1 Table 3's point estimates. Conversely, v2's drift-MSE Table 6 omits the uncertainty values reported in v1 Table 2.

E6.justification: Canonical scores change beyond the Table 1 scaling change from 10 to 100. v1 Table 3 ranks FIM-SDE above BISDE on oil and wind; v2's documented evaluation reverses those zero-shot rankings. New results include diffusion MSE, ablations and Lorenz finetuning: Table 2 reports MMD 0.403933 zero-shot versus 0.003838 finetuned for N(0,1) initial conditions. Motion results disappear. These do not establish controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The generative factorization changes from conditioning each transition term on the initial state in v1 Equation 6 to the preceding state in v2 Equation 5. v2 adds a posterior-mean optimality statement for the MSE objective, while v1's explicit alternative KL matching divergence is removed. Much of the expanded SDE and normalization mathematics restates existing material.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from zero-shot function estimation to in-context estimation plus rapid target-data adaptation. v2 explicitly restricts its stated scope to low-dimensional systems and adds claims of consistently outperforming baselines after finetuning and up to 50-fold faster adaptation. These materially revise the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes mismatched microscopic timescales as its main limitation. v2 emphasizes polynomial-prior restrictions and dimensionality, interpreting rising rejection rates as a data-generation bottleneck. It attributes weak Lorenz zero-shot performance to excessive inferred diffusion and explains finetuning as correcting that bias. New ablations support discussions of context requirements and scaling; v1's oil/wind geometric-Brownian-motion interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents a 60K validation set, dropout, activation and feed-forward widths, 1.3M pretraining steps and roughly six days of training. Appendices E–G substantially expand baseline configurations, dataset descriptions, preprocessing, splits and evaluation-grid details. v1's Julia/solver and gradient-clipping disclosures disappear. The advertised model, repository and tutorial access remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning around neural SDEs, prior-fitted networks and amortized posterior inference, adding discussions of works such as Frishman and Ronceray, Bartosh, Müller and Mittal. v1's broad first-neural/nonparametric-estimator claim is narrowed toward in-context recognition, with fuller acknowledgment of existing neural SDE approaches.

P1.justification: The title and extensive introductory, methodological and concluding prose are rewritten. The introduction gains numbered contributions, much related work moves into Appendix A, and objective-function discussion is reorganized. Appendices are restructured into separate background, baseline, metric, experiment and ablation sections. This exceeds terminology changes accompanying new scientific content.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column layout. Figure 1 gains a data-generation/pretraining panel and moves earlier. Motion forecasting and the original oil/wind function plots are removed; new Lorenz/convergence plots, real-data trajectories and a full canonical-system figure are added. Tables gain noise groupings, separate diffusion results, dataset summaries and ablation displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially closes validation gaps through direct neural-SDE comparisons, controlled robustness tests and systematic ablations, while expanded implementation and dataset documentation makes the work easier to assess and reproduce. These gains outweigh the removed motion experiment and lost drift-MSE uncertainty reporting. Important overstatements remain: Table 3's wind result favors BISDE over finetuned FIM-SDE, and iteration counts alone do not establish the claimed 50-fold compute reduction.
